:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/problem:
Calculate the product $C D,$ if
![](images/94/945664c408577aac1d1a745120b3c17c46fd9db93e6d26cc53a4e501390936e2.png)
and 
![](images/90/907ffa0b29d96249fe03a7fce3fe682c08982b14c7b7f72840540e6269196425.png)
:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/worked-solution:
Notice that $D$ is the $2$nd *column* of the identity matrix $I_3.$

Since we're multiplying the $3\times 3$ matrix $C$ by the $2$nd *column* of the identity matrix $I_3,$ the result must be the $2$nd *column* of $C.$ Therefore,

![](images/98/980ae75452824b4a8aa701b4e11be8c31448557933357458329f0a2b73a1cca6.png)

Don't believe it? Let's check the long way:

$$
\begin{aligned}CD & =\begin{bmatrix}2 & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & -4 \\ 5 & 4 & -2\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}2\cdot 0+1\cdot 1+0\cdot 0 \\ -1\cdot 0+1\cdot 1+(-4)\cdot 0 \\ 5\cdot 0+4\cdot 1+(-2)\cdot 0\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 1 \\ 4\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$
